slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: GGT transfers the γ-glutamyl group from L-γ-glutamyl-3-carboxy-4-nitroanilide to glycylglycine, releasing 2-nitro-5-aminobenzoic acid.
The rate of 2-nitro-5-aminobenzoic acid formation (405 nm) is proportional to GGT activity.
GGT is found mainly in kidney, pancreas, liver and prostate; it is used in hepatobiliary disease (biliary obstruction, cirrhosis, liver tumours).

This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “γ-GT” kit (IFU BEIS08-I, 06/06/16). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum only. GGT is stable for at least 3 days at 2–8 °C, 8 hours at 15–25 °C and 1 month at −20 °C.
R1 (buffer): TRIS pH 8.25 100 mmol/L. R2 (substrate, tablet): glycylglycine 100 mmol/L, L-γ-glutamyl-3-carboxy-4-nitroanilide 3 mmol/L.
Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 405 nm, 25/30/37 °C thermostat, 1.0 cm cuvettes.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: Working reagent: dissolve the R2 tablet (or vial) in the stated volume of R1 for your pack size (e.g. one tablet in 15 mL of R1) — the exact volume is in your kit IFU.
Working reagent stability: 21 days at 2–8 °C or 5 days at room temperature (15–25 °C). Do not use broken tablets.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: Signs of deterioration: particles, turbidity or blank absorbance at 405 nm ≥ 1.80.
The values come from the SPINREACT “γ-GT” IFU (BEIS08-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 405 nm; constant temperature 25 °C, 30 °C or 37 °C (thermostat ± 0.1 °C).
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water or air.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: working reagent 1.0 mL + sample 100 µL.
4. Mix and wait 1 minute.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Read the initial absorbance (A), start the stopwatch and read every 1 minute for 3 minutes.
6. Calculate the absorbance differences and the mean change per minute (ΔA/min).

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: GGT programme
rows: Initial A, then every 1 min for 3 min

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: GGT (U/L) = ΔA/min × 1190.
Temperature conversion (IFU table): result at 25 °C × 1.79 = 37 °C; at 30 °C × 1.30 = 37 °C.
Linear up to 375 U/L; above that, dilute the sample 1/10 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 10.
IFU reference (37 °C): women 7–32 U/L, men 11–50 U/L.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Do not use plasma — anticoagulants inhibit the enzyme.
Gross haemolysis interferes.
Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).
IFU: performance depends on the analyser used.

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and technique; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
